# Workdeck — API reference for AI agents

Workdeck is a personal workdeck of small apps: Docs, Sheets, Forms, Slides,
Draw, Files, Todo, Calendar, Kanban and Blog, all stored in one unified
account document. This file describes its HTTP API so an agent can read and
write a user's workdeck directly, without driving a browser.

## Base URL

https://workdeck-m.vercel.app

(The same host this file was fetched from. Local development uses
http://localhost:4000 with the same paths.)

## Authentication

Every request identifies the account. Send the account KEY the user gives
you — a short word or phrase they also sign in with:

    GET  /api/todo?key=<key>
    PUT  /api/todo   { "key": "<key>", "action": ..., "data": ... }

The server resolves the key to the account; you never handle a password or
a hash. Whoever holds the key can read and write everything in the
workdeck, so treat it as a secret.

Finding the key:
  1. Check for WORKDECK_KEY=<key> in the .env file (or environment) where
     YOU (the agent) are running. If it is there, use it — don't ask again.
  2. If not, ask the user for their Workdeck key (Workdeck -> Settings ->
     View My Key shows it). Once you have it, save it as
     WORKDECK_KEY=<key> in the .env file in your working folder so future
     sessions find it without asking. Pasting it in the chat also works.

Shortcut for long sessions: a login returns the account's `hash`, which you
may send instead of the key for the rest of the session (the browser
front-end works this way):

    POST /api/users   { "key": "<key>", "action": "login" }   -> { hash, data }

Don't save the hash to .env — the key is the durable credential.

Changing the key (only when the user asks): this moves the whole account to
the new key, keeping every app's data. The old key stops working
immediately:

    POST /api/workdeck  { "key": "<current key>", "action": "changeKey",
                          "data": { "newKey": "<new key>" } }
         -> { "hash": "<new hash>", "data": <account document> }

(/api/users takes the same call, and `hash` may be sent instead of `key`.)
Afterwards save the new key as WORKDECK_KEY in your .env — the old one no
longer logs in. A new key that already has an account is refused.

Data only: use the key for the operations the user asked for, and never
create or delete accounts.

## Conventions

- JSON in, JSON out. Nearly everything is:
      GET  /api/<app>                 -> read the account's data
      PUT  /api/<app>   { action, data } -> mutate
- Responses: { "success": true, ... } or { "success": false, "error": "..." }.
- Successful mutations return `data`: the ENTIRE unified account document as
  saved. Use it as your fresh read — no second GET needed.
- Send `key` with every request: query parameter on GET, `key` field in the
  JSON body on mutations. After a login you may send `hash` instead —
  see Authentication.
- DateTimes are local floating strings without timezone: "2026-11-02T08:40".
  All-day calendar events: "2026-11-02" with allDay: true.
- IDs are server-generated short strings. Reuse IDs from GET responses.
- The account document is one JSON blob per app section; each app endpoint
  only saves the sections it owns. Send each mutation to the endpoint of the
  app that owns the data.
- Keep documents under ~1 MB (larger payloads are gzipped automatically, but
  there is a hard ceiling — Filebox file bytes especially).

## Account document shape (what GET returns)

    {
      docs:     [ { id, title, content, contentType, tagId, pinned, archived,
                    sharedId?, createdAt, updatedAt } ],   // Docs
      tags:     [ { id, name, color } ],
      sheets:   [ ... ],   // Sheets spreadsheets (Univer data)
      forms:    [ ... ],   // Forms + linked sheet info
      slides:   [ ... ],   // Slides decks
      draws:    [ ... ],   // Draw canvases
      files:    [ { id, name, mime, size, folderId, tags, storageKey, ... } ],
      folders:  [ { id, name, parentId, tags, ... } ],
      todo:     [ { id, name, items: [ { id, title, description?, dueDate?,
                    priority?, completed?, createdAt } ], createdAt, updatedAt } ],
      calendars:[ { id, name, color, visible, tagId, createdAt, updatedAt } ],
      events:   [ { id, calId, title, description?, location?, start, end,
                    allDay, rrule?, exdates?, overrides?, reminders?, links?,
                    createdAt, updatedAt } ],
      kanban:   [ { id, name, columns: [...], rows: [...], cards: [...],
                    links: [...], createdAt, updatedAt } ],
      posts:    [ { id, title, slug, path, html, excerpt, tagId,
                    publishedAt, createdAt, updatedAt } ],   // Blog
      settings: { theme, viewMode, lastOpened, blog: { title, description,
                    address: { slug, publishedAt } | null }, ... }
    }

## Endpoints

### Todo  —  /api/todo
    GET  -> { todo: [lists], settings, ... }
    PUT  { action: "createList",   data: { name?, id? } }
    PUT  { action: "renameList",   data: { listId, name } }
    PUT  { action: "updateList",   data: { listId, list: { name, items: [...] } } }
         (upserts the whole list; items are the full item array)
    PUT  { action: "deleteList",   data: { listId } }
    PUT  { action: "updateSettings", data: { settings: {...} } }

### Calendar  —  /api/calendar
    GET  -> { calendars: [...], events: [...], settings, ... }
    PUT  { action: "createCalendar", data: { name?, color? } }
    PUT  { action: "updateCalendar", data: { calId, updates: { name?, color?,
                                               visible?, tagId? } } }
    PUT  { action: "deleteCalendar", data: { calId } }
         (deletes the calendar and all its events)
    PUT  { action: "createEvent",  data: { event: { calId, title, start, end,
             description?, location?, allDay?, rrule? } } }
    PUT  { action: "updateEvent",  data: { eventId, event: {...} } }
    PUT  { action: "deleteEvent",  data: { eventId } }
    Recurrence is stored verbatim in `rrule` (RFC 5545 string) — the API never
    expands recurrences; clients do.

### Kanban  —  /api/kanban
    GET  -> { kanban: [boards], settings, ... }
    PUT  { action: "createBoard",  data: { name?, id? } }
         (new board gets default columns: To Do / In Progress / Done)
    PUT  { action: "renameBoard",  data: { boardId, name } }
    PUT  { action: "updateBoard",  data: { boardId, board: {...} } }
         (upserts the whole board record: columns, rows, cards, links —
          read the board first, mutate, write back)
    PUT  { action: "deleteBoard",  data: { boardId } }
    Card records live in board.cards; their exact shape comes from GET.

### Blog  —  /api/blog
    GET  -> { posts: [posts], settings, ... }
    PUT  { action: "createPost",        data: { title?, tagId?, id? } }
    PUT  { action: "updatePost",        data: { id, title?, html?, tagId? } }
         (html is Quill HTML, scrubbed server-side; unpublished posts keep
          a title-derived slug suggestion in `slug`)
    PUT  { action: "deletePost",        data: { id } }
    PUT  { action: "updateBlogSettings",data: { title? } }
    PUT  { action: "publishPost",       data: { id, slug } } -> { blog: { postUrl, path } }
         (makes one post public at /<slug> — the slug is chosen per publish,
          unique across all accounts; unpublish/delete frees it again.
          Posts published before per-post links keep /<address>/<post>)
    PUT  { action: "unpublishPost",     data: { id } }
    PUT  { action: "updateSettings",    data: { settings: {...} } }

### Sheets  —  /api/users
    GET  -> { sheets: [...], settings, ... }
    PUT  { action: "updateSheet",  data: { sheetId, sheetData } }
    PUT  { action: "deleteSheet",  data: { sheetId } }
    PUT  { action: "shareSheet",   data: { sheetId } }  -> { shareUrl }
    sheetData is the full spreadsheet document (Univer format) — read first.

### Forms  —  /api/forms
    GET  -> { forms: [...], settings, ... }
    PUT  { action: "updateForm",      data: { formId, formData } }
    PUT  { action: "deleteForm",      data: { formId } }
    PUT  { action: "shareForm",       data: { formId } }  -> { shareUrl }
    PUT  { action: "getResponses",    data: { formId } }  -> responses
    PUT  { action: "deleteResponses", data: { formId } }
    PUT  { action: "linkSheet",       data: { formId, sheetId? } }
    PUT  { action: "unlinkSheet",     data: { formId } }
    Public (no auth): POST { action: "submitResponse", shareId,
                             data: { response } }

### Slides  —  /api/slides
    GET  -> { slides: [decks], settings, ... }
    PUT  { action: "updateDeck",   data: { deckId, deckData } }
    PUT  { action: "deleteDeck",   data: { deckId } }
    PUT  { action: "shareDeck",    data: { deckId } }  -> { shareUrl }

### Draw  —  /api/draw
    GET  -> { draws: [drawings], settings, ... }
    PUT  { action: "updateDrawing", data: { drawingId, drawingData } }
    PUT  { action: "deleteDrawing", data: { drawingId } }
    PUT  { action: "shareDrawing",  data: { drawingId } }  -> { shareUrl }

### Files —  /api/filebox
    GET            -> whole document (files + folders metadata)
    GET ?fileId=X  -> the file's raw bytes (binary response)
    PUT  { action: "uploadFile", data: { name, mime, base64, folderId?, tags? } }
         base64-encoded content; a few hundred KB max by default.

### Workdeck launchpad  —  /api/workdeck
    GET  -> whole document (everything above)
    PUT  { action: "createDoc",      data: { title?, content?, contentType?,
                                             tagId? } }
    PUT  { action: "createSheet",    data: { name?, tagId? } }   (stub)
    PUT  { action: "createForm",     data: { name?, tagId? } }   (stub)
    PUT  { action: "createDeck",     data: { name?, tagId? } }   (stub)
    PUT  { action: "createTodo",     data: { name?, tagId? } }   (stub list)
    PUT  { action: "createKanban",   data: { name?, tagId? } }   (stub board)
    PUT  { action: "createPost",     data: { title?, tagId? } }  (stub post)
    PUT  { action: "createDrawing",  data: { name?, tagId? } }   (stub)
    PUT  { action: "createCalendar", data: { name?, tagId? } }   (stub)
    PUT  { action: "createTag",      data: { name, color? } }
    PUT  { action: "recordOpen",     data: { fileId, app } }   (recency)
    PUT  { action: "renameFile",     data: { fileId, name, app? } }
    PUT  { action: "deleteFile",     data: { fileId, app } }
    PUT  { action: "createFolder",   data: { name, parentId? } }
    PUT  { action: "updateSettings", data: { settings: {...} } }

### Docs  —  /api/docs   (fetch-style: GET/PUT/DELETE; POST is login/create-account)
    GET              -> { docs: [...], tags: [...], settings, ... }
    GET ?shared=X    -> public shared doc
    PUT  { action: "createDoc",    data: { title?, content?, contentType?,
                                            tagId? } }
    PUT  { action: "updateDoc",    data: { docId, updates: {...} } }
    PUT  { action: "deleteDoc",    data: { docId } }
    PUT  { action: "shareDoc",     data: { docId } }     -> { shareUrl }
    PUT  { action: "togglePin",    data: { docId } }
    PUT  { action: "toggleArchive",data: { docId } }
    PUT  { action: "createTag",    data: { name, color? } }
    PUT  { action: "updateTag",    data: { tagId, updates: {...} } }
    PUT  { action: "deleteTag",    data: { tagId } }
    contentType: "plain-text" or "markdown".

### Published posts  —  /api/site   (NO AUTH — read-only)
Posts published from the Blog app are readable at /<post-slug> (the slug
chosen at publish, unique across accounts). Posts published before
per-post links keep the blog-home shape: /<address> lists them and
/<address>/<post-slug> reads one. The slug resolves server-side to the
owning account; the account key/hash is never involved or exposed. There
are no write methods — everything but GET answers 405.

    GET ?slug=<post-slug>        -> { site: { slug, publishedAt },
                                      blog: { title, description },
                                      post: { ..., html } }
    GET ?slug=<address>          -> { ..., posts: [ { id, title, slug,
                                      excerpt, publishedAt } ] }   (legacy)
    GET ?slug=<address>&post=<slug> -> { ..., post: { ..., html } } (legacy)

Projection rules: only posts with publishedAt set appear, newest first
in lists, without html (fetch one article at a time). Everything else in
the account — drafts, docs, files, settings — never leaves the server.

## Examples

Add three tasks to a new todo list:

    curl -X PUT https://workdeck-m.vercel.app/api/todo \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"key":"<key>","action":"createList","data":{"name":"Errands","items":[]}}'

Then, using the list `id` from the response:

    curl -X PUT https://workdeck-m.vercel.app/api/todo \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"key":"<key>","action":"updateList","data":{"listId":"<id>","list":{"name":"Errands","items":[{"id":"i1","title":"Buy milk","completed":false}]}}}'

Create a calendar event:

    curl -X PUT https://workdeck-m.vercel.app/api/calendar \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"key":"<key>","action":"createEvent","data":{"event":{"calId":"<calId>","title":"Dentist","start":"2026-11-04T14:30","end":"2026-11-04T15:00"}}}'

## Notes for agents

- Prefer create-then-update (createList with empty items, then updateList)
  when adding many tasks in one list.
- When a user asks "add X to my Workdeck", pick the app they mean; when
  unsure, ask the user.
- Failed writes return success:false with a readable error — surface it.
- Human-facing documentation: /docs
